nodes.claim: The perfect display is one geometry per level, not one per screen: every population cut — circle, city, country, world — is the same between-person space, at one declared cohort-independent projection, with a different cohort drawn, so zooming changes who is drawn and never what distance means; the person's own occasions are a second geometry, and the seam between the two lies at the person.
nodes.detail: Revised 2026-09-02: the 2026-08-25 seed said 'one geometry that every scale shares' and was wrong by exactly one level — the program's hierarchical consensus (cen-1's two-geometry revision on tst-6/tst-7; pat-3; map-6/map-7) holds that between-person structure does not carry within-person structure, so the seed assumed ergodicity silently. THE GEOMETRY. Coordinates: the between-person system cen-1 publishes at model level — directions plus population-level sufficient statistics reproducing couplings with their uncertainty, never a table of person scores — of which the product's nightly loadings doc is the shipped, uncertainty-free ancestor; every axiom enters through its own measurement model, so an axiom is a set of directions in the shared space, never a separate screen, and the instrument space embeds in it (tst-6). Distance: one meaning at every stop — in this node's restatement, the model's expected disagreement between two points beyond popularity (the People lens's own sentence is quoted at map-2). Zoom is a FILTER on this fixed space, never a re-fit: the population stops are the same coordinates with a different cohort drawn, so distance semantics are invariant under zoom in the PUBLISHED BASIS, at one fit (the time axis between fits is map-3's, priced separately). The invariance does not survive projection for free: any cohort-dependent layout — a force plane, a per-cohort PCA; InSight's planeOf is one (map-3) — re-earns the metaphor switch in the drawn plane, so the perfect display fixes the projection too: one declared, cohort-independent plane of the shared basis, the object this run's bridge request is declared over. A per-cohort embedding would make distance mean 'this cohort's structure' at each stop — a silent metaphor switch (map-2), a stability loss (map-3), the loss of the comparison the Mirror exists to draw. A cohort whose loadings differ is graded by a named invariance method (que-4: exact, partial, approximate, alignment); the frame draws only the comparisons that grade licenses, labeled — where graded comparability fails, the shared-space distance stops meaning the same thing for that cohort and the display says so rather than drawing it. Direction: unnamed, explained by items (map-2's landscape-metaphor negative); the items are the fixed landmarks, the crowd is what changes — also the orientation aid a thin cohort needs (map-11's navigation literature). The level-of-detail ladder is map-13; below the person the geometry changes (map-12); channel arbitration (mark type for level of detail, object type for geometry level, fill for evidential weight) is deferred to map-2's table with that assignment proposed. InSight's live shadow is the strongest case for the rule: the telescope runs four distances — per-answer unusualness at You (live for age and edu only, D99; refused for the rest, D72), test-score likeness at Near and City (answer agreement as City's fallback), axis-score distance to place averages at Country and World, model-expected disagreement in the People lens (docs/MIRROR.md §2, PEOPLE-MAP on main) — and PEOPLE-MAP §6's planned plane switch, a re-solve over a filtered pool whose 'who teleports' reading is a feature, is the case this rule bites hardest: that reading is per-cohort structure this node says must be drawn as a declared difference inside one basis. The disagreement is this node's. Search record at map-10: no source states the per-level invariance; no study tests readers across an individuals-to-density switch. Falsifier, biting the design half, not map-2's normative half: readers asked what a city's structure says about the world's, given two cohorts in one published basis at a fixed plane versus two per-cohort re-fits side by side — this node fails if the re-fits yield more correct cross-cohort statements. Status argued: the composition is this lane's; its premises wear cited one node over (map-2, map-3, map-11) or by edge (tst-7, map-7).

nodes.claim: Distance means exactly one thing per view — and so does every other channel the frame contains; a display that mixes meanings in one frame is wrong regardless of how it tests.
nodes.detail: Raised argued→cited 2026-08-26; adversarially checked the same run. The rule itself is normative — a claim about what a display owes its reader, not a prediction — so the empirical spatialization literature grounds the PREMISE the rule rests on: every channel present in a frame gets read, whether or not the designer assigned it a meaning. (1) Viewers default to straight-line metric distance: across display types there is no significant difference between 'default' and 'direct' distance instructions — people interpret default distance instructions as direct straight-line distance (Fabrikant & Montello 2008, the strongest single result here). The 2004 network-display study is cited for its design, which explicitly separated direct Euclidean distance, cumulative path length, topological hop count and link visual variables as competing 'distances' (Fabrikant et al. 2004); its effect direction is deliberately not asserted — full text was unreachable this run and secondary summaries conflict. (2) The mapping from distance to MEANING is not automatic, and competing visual structure overrides distance when present: the first-law experiments 'largely support' distance-as-similarity while finding non-distance display characteristics also move similarity judgments (Montello et al. 2003); when regions are drawn, region membership largely determines judged similarity, beating metric distance, with hue modifying it further (Fabrikant, Montello & Mark 2006); and the information-landscape metaphor is an outright negative result — the metaphor is not self-evident to lay users (Fabrikant, Montello & Mark 2010). Two consequences this node draws as its OWN design inferences, downstream of that premise: (a) the semantic table this node demands must cover every channel the frame contains, and the perfect display omits channels it has no assigned meaning for; (b) one carve-out, forced by map-4's evidence: a channel may carry its one meaning plus a DECLARED modifier of that meaning's evidential weight — uncertainty-about-X drawn by suppressing X's own channel (the value-suppressing-palette pattern) is one composite semantic, stated in the table, not a second meaning smuggled into the frame. What the rule forbids is unassigned or double-booked meaning, not declared composite meaning. InSight's live shadow: the People lens states its distance out loud ('the model's expected disagreement between two people, beyond each question's popularity' — docs/PEOPLE-MAP.md on main); this node says the rest of any frame owes the same sentence. Verification grade: all five sources verified at abstract level against multiple independent indexes, re-checked by a separate adversarial pass; no within-study numbers are asserted.
sources: Montello DR, Fabrikant SI, Ruocco M, Middleton RS 2003, 'Testing the First Law of Cognitive Geography on Point-Display Spatializations', COSIT 2003, LNCS 2825:316-331, DOI 10.1007/978-3-540-39923-0_21

Fabrikant SI, Montello DR, Ruocco M, Middleton RS 2004, 'The Distance-Similarity Metaphor in Network-Display Spatializations', Cartography and Geographic Information Science 31(4):237-252, DOI 10.1559/1523040042742402 — cited for design; effect direction not asserted (full text unreachable, secondary summaries conflict)

nodes.claim: Authored anchors and learned embedding combine in ONE persistent space: stability must be structural — the space itself persists and updates incrementally — never post-hoc alignment, and it is a measured trade-off, not a free win.
nodes.detail: Raised conjecture→cited 2026-08-26; adversarially checked the same run. The claim is refined by the evidence in three ways. First, the seed's premise ('a re-fit teleports everything and destroys spatial memory') traces to Misue et al. 1995, which introduced the mental map and its three formal models (orthogonal ordering, proximity, topology) as an ASSUMPTION, not a finding — the paper is conceptual/algorithmic — and twenty years of experiments then made the picture conditional: stability demonstrably helps orientation and route-finding in an evolving layout — significantly faster, fewer errors, holding as the number of targets increases (Archambault & Purchase, GD 2012) — which is precisely the Map's task class (a space the user learns, leaves, and re-enters), while for general dynamic-graph comprehension 'no experiment has found conclusive evidence that supports the effectiveness of the mental map' (Archambault & Purchase 2013, their own summary), early tests confirmed the assumption only for some task categories (Purchase, Hoggan & Görg 2007), and one study found simple mental-map preservation no better than optimizing static aesthetics per frame (Saffrey & Purchase 2008). Second, the effect is non-monotonic: graph sequences with HIGH or LOW mental-map preservation both beat MEDIUM preservation (Purchase & Samra 2008, 'Extremes Are Better'; the authors themselves read the U-shape partly as individual preference). Read by analogy — that study varied an algorithmic preservation parameter, not anchoring — this node treats half-pinning as the medium case and argues anchoring must be structural, not cosmetic; the transfer is this node's own inference, recorded as such. Third, on mechanism the projection literature agrees and prices it: dynamic t-SNE adds an explicit movement penalty λ, an explicitly controllable trade-off between temporal coherence and per-step projection reliability in which strong pinning costs fidelity (Rauber et al. 2016); that trade-off has since been formally defined and measured — Vernier et al. 2020 contribute spatial and temporal stability metrics plus benchmarks for exactly this property — and guided variants steer points with global anchors (Vernier et al. 2021, PCD-tSNE/LD-tSNE: learned positions pinned to stable guides, peer-reviewed). Two results push the mechanism one step past the seed. Re-fit-then-align — the orthogonal-Procrustes recipe used at scale by Hamilton et al. 2016 — is itself a documented noise source in diachronic word embeddings, transferred here by analogy: Dubossarsky et al. 2019 show alignment noise corrupts downstream measurement and a formulation that never fits separate spaces outperforms alignment models on synthetic and manual test sets. And a learned parametric map supports fast online embedding of new data (Sainburg, McInnes & Gentner 2021) — that new points can land without moving old ones, because nothing re-fits, is this node's inference from that mechanism. So the perfect layout is not 'learned, then pinned back'; it is one persistent space, incrementally updated, whose per-update movement is a published, budgeted quantity — the display-side analogue of pat-2's auditability, which is what the depends edge now means. Tooling note recorded so no later run cites it wrongly: AlignedUMAP, the obvious off-the-shelf tool, has NO method paper by its author's own statement (umap-learn GitHub discussion #966, read at full text this run and re-read by the adversarial pass) — software-docs grade; the peer-reviewed neighbors are 2-MAP (Liu et al., WACV 2020) and the Rauber/Vernier line. Verification grade: abstract-level for all sources except the two GitHub items (full text); numeric effect sizes were not recoverable this run and none are asserted. Product note, code-verified first-party 2026-08-28: the shipped nightly fit already implements this node's structural half IN LOADING SPACE — one persistent model folded forward (functions/src/patterns.ts, runPatternsFit: getModel → fold → putModel, idempotent by lastDay, consecutive publishes sharing one continuous basis) — so incremental persistence is the product's architecture, not a proposal; the drawn plane a reader's spatial memory actually attaches to is a nonlinear, partly discontinuous device-side function of that basis (patternsMap.ts: seed, springs, declutter) and stays unmeasured, which is exactly what D325's space:'loading' declaration says. And this lane's displacement request crossed the bridge 2026-08-27 as D325 (the bridge's first crossing): the fit now publishes a per-publish displacement summary on v2_patterns/loadings — loading-space L2 over the published 4 dp vectors, publish-to-publish, deliberately unaligned per the verdict's correction, space stated on the doc because drawn-plane displacement is a different (nonlinear) number. 'Published' is therefore real; 'budgeted' is not yet (nothing consumes the number as a threshold). Path to measured: §4 defines the rung against numbers readable from main, and the doc lives only in Firestore — the 2026-08-28 REQUESTS row (committed fit-scorecard snapshot) is what would let this node rise on a real displacement distribution.

nodes.claim: Uncertainty is geometry, not a footnote: the perfect display makes thin data LOOK thin — outcome uncertainty, encoded frequency-framed in the mark itself.
nodes.detail: Raised argued→cited 2026-08-26 in a narrowed form; adversarially checked the same run (the check corrected four framing errors here before landing — see LOG). Two separable findings, and keeping them separate is the narrowing. HOW to draw uncertainty (encoding form): (1) the default encoding actively misleads — a bar depicting a mean induces within-the-bar bias, points inside the bar judged more likely than points equidistant from the mean outside it (Newman & Scholl 2012), and viewers misinterpret bar+error-bar displays at even basic levels while gradient and violin encodings leave judgments better informed by the margin of error (Correll & Gleicher 2014); (2) making the mark itself carry the evidence changes decisions — value-suppressing uncertainty palettes allocate less of the color channel to values as uncertainty grows, thin data literally drawn less distinguishable, and a crowdsourced evaluation found they push people to weight uncertainty more heavily in decisions (Correll, Moritz & Heer 2018); in an incentivized transit task, 50-quantile dotplots were the best-performing display: +4.4 percentage points of optimal payoff attained versus the no-uncertainty control on the final trial (95% credible interval 2.1–8.3 pp), with 3.9 pp lower performance SD (CI 2.4–5.7 pp), from the authors' Bayesian beta regression — while the advantage over CDFs was not reliably distinguished (1.3 pp, CI −0.1 to 3.2) (Fernandes et al. 2018, the one study this run verified at full text from the authors' published analysis); (3) the frequency/discrete-draw framing beats static density summaries — hypothetical outcome plots outperform error bars and violins for inferences about ordering across two and three quantities, with the advantage concentrated in those multi-quantity questions (Hullman, Resnick & Adar 2015); animated HOPs beat conventional static uncertainty displays for trend judgment (Kale et al. 2019); count-based quantile dotplots beat densities for everyday probabilistic estimates on small screens (Kay et al. 2016). These encoding-form results were largely demonstrated on inferential-uncertainty displays (margins of error) and transfer across uncertainty types as findings about form. WHICH uncertainty to draw is orthogonal, and is where the seed over-claimed: drawing INFERENTIAL uncertainty correctly can inflate perceived effects — 95% confidence intervals made people overestimate and overpay for treatment effects relative to prediction intervals (Hofman et al. 2020) — so the perfect display's 'thin' is outcome/predictive uncertainty: the spread of what actually happens, not the precision of a mean. Recorded so no later run re-inflates the seed: geometry does not beat text per se — in the transit ranking, plain-text quantile intervals outranked the PDF and interval displays on point estimates, though those orderings are not reliably distinguished; ensembles are not automatically honest — summary-cone and spaghetti displays of identical hurricane data produce different interpretations (Padilla, Ruginski & Creem-Regehr 2017, whose ensemble displays also over-weight individual members; Ruginski et al. 2016 for different decisions under different visual properties); a correctly drawn interval can be re-read as deterministic bounds — the deterministic construal error (Savelli & Joslyn's line of work, reviewed in Joslyn & Savelli 2021); one map-decision study found mixed accuracy effects — sometimes improved, sometimes unchanged — alongside strategy shifts (Korporaal et al. 2020); and the field's own methodologists warn the genre is noisy — practiced authors omit uncertainty deliberately, citing credibility costs (Hullman 2020, survey of 90 authors), and only 10 of 39 studies claiming to identify biased behavior gave participants enough information to identify the normative decision (Hullman, Kale & Hartline 2025). The perfect display therefore encodes outcome uncertainty as frequency-framed geometry of the mark itself — draws, dots, suppressed palettes — extending InSight's n=0-draws-nothing refusal continuously; states WHICH uncertainty it drew; and never treats 'uncertainty shown' as 'honesty achieved'. Per map-2's carve-out, a suppressed palette is a declared modifier of a channel's one meaning, stated in the view's semantic table — that is what the supports edge asserts. Verification grade: Fernandes 2018 at full text (authors' analysis file, figures confirmed to the digit by the adversarial pass); all others abstract-level against multiple independent indexes; MacEachren et al. 2012 (Visual Semiotics & Uncertainty Visualization, IEEE TVCG 18(12):2496-2505, DOI 10.1109/TVCG.2012.279) is real and relevant but its performance results could not be verified this run, so its intuitiveness rankings are deliberately not cited.

nodes.claim: Efficiency is a display property, not an implementation detail: the perfect map is drawn on a phone from published, cacheable aggregates over the declared plane of the fixed space — binned counts, never per-person rows — with per-view work bounded by display resolution rather than record count and no blocking round trip inside the interaction loop, a transfer from desktop visual-analysis findings to the phone's network loop that this lane makes by analogy.
nodes.detail: Revised 2026-09-02; the 2026-08-25 form said 'no per-view server work' and the systems literature does not support that absolute — it supports per-view work made small and bounded (map-14, cited: added latency changed exploration and discovery on the desktop; blocking, not slowness, is what the evidence condemns; binned aggregation bounds cost by the resolution of the visualized data rather than the record count, in reported wording). The adversarial pass held this node at argued rather than letting it rise: the premises are cited one node over, and the composition — therefore the phone draws from published bins with no blocking round trip — is this lane's design conclusion, the same shape map-6 was demoted for on 2026-09-01. WHAT THE CONCLUSION ADDS TO ITS PREMISES. The literature's own systems (map-14: Nanocubes, Falcon) keep a bounded server in the loop; the perfect map's zero is a design choice argued from map-1's fixed space and fixed plane: zoom is a filter, so the world-scale bins are one published artifact per fit, cacheable for the session like the loadings doc is today, and the phone only draws (map-13's density level). No mobile visual-analysis latency study was found (map-10), so the transfer from desktop findings to a phone's network round trip is by analogy and the claim string says so. The auditability half of the seed — anyone can recompute the picture from the same public numbers — stands as this lane's inference on pat-2's recompute contract; no published argument for it was found (map-10). InSight's live shadow: the loadings doc is one read per session and the layout runs on the device (docs/PEOPLE-MAP.md §1 on main); the whole-world map was deferred there (§7) on four reasons — a per-person positions doc's size, its erasure obligation, night-to-night rotation, and that publishing a per-person derived summary is a new presentation of people and an owner call — and the binned artifact this node prescribes answers the first two by construction, meets the third on the fit's persistent basis, and leaves the fourth exactly where §7 put it: with the owner (REQUESTS 2026-09-02, which files it as a bounded new exposure at cell grain, not as none). Falsifier, with map-1's task: readers asked what a city's structure says about the world's read no worse from a phone whose every redraw waits on a bounded server than from one drawing published bins — the zero would then be cost, not display, and this node would fall to map-14's premises alone.

nodes.claim: A drawn cross-axis connection declares its population, its decomposition and its basis, and draws between-person and within-person coupling as different geometries — declaration is structure, not courtesy.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-28 as this lane's answer to the charter's cross-connection mandate (§1); FISSIONED 2026-09-01 on central's 2026-08-28 question (carrying go-7): the original node bundled two cited premises, a cited precedent survey and this lane's own design inferences under one status at ~1531 words, handing the skeptic no target smaller than the whole essay. The evidence now lives where the ladder can grip it — the level divergence at map-7 (cited), the reading unreliability at map-8 (cited), the deployed-system precedent at map-9 (cited), the two search-negatives at map-10 (argued — an absence a search can attack but no source can ground) — and this node keeps what was always this lane's own: the rule and its consequences, at the rung an inference honestly wears. The demotion cited→argued is the fission's point, not a loss: every sentence that earned cited still wears it, one node over. The form now differs from map-2's on purpose: map-2 wears cited because its premise sources sit in its own node; map-6's premises moved out, so its rung covers exactly what remains in it — the inference (fission map-2 the same way and its rule half would wear argued too). Forwarding note: the Fisher rebuttal and the per-pair scope note live at map-7, the search-negatives at map-10 — four sibling nodes (pat-3, cen-1, cen-2, cen-7) still cite map-6 for content or a rung that moved this run; they are named in this run's LOG row for their owners to repair. The sibling axioms each reached the same shape of answer at their own rungs (statuses as of 2026-09-01): an honest coupling is published with its decomposition (gen-11 cited, bod-8 cited), exchanged as statistics carrying their basis (db-6 argued), and split by level because between-person structure does not carry within-person structure (tst-6 argued, on tst-7 cited) — this node is the last mile: the drawn connection either preserves those declarations into the frame or undoes the axioms' honesty at the moment of reading. THE RULE'S WARRANT, from the premises: map-7 says the level split is real and per-pair; map-8 says reading a drawn connection is demonstrably unreliable in both directions; map-10 records that no study shows readers recover an undeclared population or level unaided. That absence is load-bearing: if readers could be shown to recover the population unaided, declaration would be courtesy; nothing shows they can, so it is structure — the frame carries the population rather than trusting the reader to infer it. The product-shaped worry — that a Mirror user reads the crowd's coupling as their own — is this lane's inference from map-7's divergence plus InSight's juxtaposition of you and cohorts, stated as inference. DESIGN CONSEQUENCES, this lane's own inferences, marked as such. (a) Population and basis enter map-2's semantic table as part of a channel's ONE meaning: even the People lens's stated sentence — 'the model's expected disagreement between two people, beyond each question's popularity' — is incomplete until it says between whom: which population, computed over what n — the same completion db-6 demands of the stored join. (b) Between-person and within-person couplings take DIFFERENT geometries — crowd structure as a field over people, your own coupling as a trajectory over time — never the same mark shape, so the population declaration is carried by form rather than by a caption a reader can skip; per map-2's premise every channel present gets read, and identical marks assert identical objects. (c) The drawn coupling states its decomposition status exactly as gen-11 and bod-8 demand of the published one: an undecomposed composite drawn as one clean connector is the display asserting a mechanism nobody measured; where the decomposition exists the mark can carry it (the comet-chart pattern map-8 records), and where it does not, the connection draws as explicitly composite — map-4's thin-data discipline applied to edges instead of positions. (d) Language is a legitimate display channel for a coupling, and for low-n within-person couplings plausibly the honest one — map-9's deployed precedent — with map-8's tension held openly: text drew the HIGHEST causality ratings in Xiong's comparison, so language is not automatically safer; its honesty has to come from stating population and basis in the sentence, which is precisely what a sentence can do and an unlabeled mark cannot.

nodes.claim: Aggregate-level and individual-level associations diverge — to the point of sign reversal — and between-person structure cannot be assumed to carry within-person structure: ergodicity suffices but is rarely met, and its necessity is contested; which decomposition exists is a per-pair fact.
nodes.detail: Fissioned out of map-6 on 2026-09-01 (central's 2026-08-28 question, carrying go-7); the evidence text is map-6's 2026-08-28 premise one, adversarially checked before it first landed, carried here with its grades intact. The level divergence is well documented — in the statistics and methodology literature rather than the visualization literature (the distinction matters and is kept; the aggregate-versus-constituent half is established, the between-versus-within-person half rests on one empirical paper plus a theoretical manifesto and carries a published rebuttal, cited below with it). Aggregate-unit versus individual: ecological and individual correlations diverge to the point of sign reversal — Robinson's nativity×illiteracy illustration runs about −0.53 across states against about +0.12 across persons (decimals from two peer-reviewed secondary commentaries, snippet grade; the original was not opened — 2026-08-28 search), and his race×illiteracy series collapses 0.946→0.773→0.203 from census divisions to states to persons without a sign flip — and Robinson is cited here for exactly this aggregate-versus-constituent point, NOT for the within-person axis, which is a different distinction (the mis-cite a careless reader would make; recorded so no later run makes it). Subgroup reversal is common enough in psychology to need a practical guide, and the authors' review judgment — typically producing incorrect interpretations, most likely when inferring across levels of analysis — is cited as review claim, not measured error rate (Kievit et al. 2013). Between-person versus within-person proper: results on inter-individual variation generalize to intra-individual variation only under ergodicity conditions rarely met by psychological processes (Molenaar 2004 — a theoretical manifesto, cited as warrant not evidence); empirically, across six repeated-measures samples, variance around the expected value ran two to four times larger within individuals than within groups, with some central-tendency agreement conceded (Fisher, Medaglia & Jeronimus 2018, their construction quoted; a published PNAS critique — ergodicity is sufficient but not necessary for generalizability — is carried alongside, so the boundary is cited with its rebuttal); and within-person and between-person effects of a time-varying covariate are distinct estimands a longitudinal model must disaggregate (Curran & Bauer 2011). Scope note, this lane's own: which decomposition applies is itself per-pair — a genotype does not vary within a person, so gene–trait couplings have no within-person half and their declaration is gen-11's direct/nurture/mating split instead; body–trait and question–question couplings carry both levels; the declaration therefore names the decomposition that exists for that pair, not a fixed template. Verification grade: all sources corroborated at search-index/abstract/snippet level against at least two independent index records (publisher full texts egress-blocked from this container, per the body and database lanes' precedent), grades labeled inline where they matter; Robinson's decimals are secondary-commentary snippet grade.
sources: Robinson WS 1950, 'Ecological Correlations and the Behavior of Individuals', American Sociological Review 15(3):351-357, DOI 10.2307/2087176 — cited for aggregate-vs-constituent only, NOT within-person; decimals snippet-grade via two IJE commentaries (PMC2663721; IJE 40(4):1123)

Molenaar PCM 2004, 'A Manifesto on Psychology as Idiographic Science: Bringing the Person Back Into Scientific Psychology, This Time Forever', Measurement: Interdisciplinary Research and Perspectives 2(4):201-218, DOI 10.1207/s15366359mea0204_1 — theoretical warrant, not empirical evidence

Fisher AJ, Medaglia JD, Jeronimus BF 2018, 'Lack of group-to-individual generalizability is a threat to human subjects research', PNAS 115(27):E6106-E6115, DOI 10.1073/pnas.1711978115, PMID 29915059 — variance around the expected value two to four times larger within individuals than within groups; a PNAS critique exists and is carried with it (DOI 10.1073/pnas.1818675116, 'Ergodicity is sufficient but not necessary')

Kievit RA, Frankenhuis WE, Waldorp LJ, Borsboom D 2013, 'Simpson's paradox in psychological science: a practical guide', Frontiers in Psychology 4:513, DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2013.00513, PMID 23964259, PMC3740239 — review/practical guide, not a measured error rate

Curran PJ, Bauer DJ 2011, 'The Disaggregation of Within-Person and Between-Person Effects in Longitudinal Models of Change', Annual Review of Psychology 62:583-619, DOI 10.1146/annurev.psych.093008.100356, PMID 19575624 — scope: time-varying covariates; a genotype has no within-person half

nodes.claim: Reading a drawn connection is unreliable in both directions — aggregation raises perceived causality, sample size is underweighted and disconfirming evidence weighed more heavily than confirming, the fused form is misread more than the plain one — and no tested design fixes it.
nodes.detail: Fissioned out of map-6 on 2026-09-01 (central's 2026-08-28 question, carrying go-7); the evidence text is map-6's 2026-08-28 premise two, adversarially checked before it first landed, carried here with its grades intact; the parked lead's disposition lives at map-10 with the negatives. From identical correlational data, more aggregated presentations elicit more causal readings — in the first experiment causality ratings were highest for plain text and bar graphs and weaker for scatter plots, and the later experiments isolate the driver: aggregating data into larger categories raised perceived causality (Xiong et al. 2020; Exps 2–3 not read at full text — 2026-08-28 search — so the encoding-versus-aggregation decomposition is carried as the authors' summary, not re-derived). The error is not one-signed: scored against a Bayesian normative benchmark, people are insensitive to sample size — systematically underweighting it — and are more sensitive to evidence disconfirming an effect than to evidence confirming it, and no tested visualization design reliably beat plain text contingency tables (Kale, Wu & Hullman 2022) — so the honest joint reading, recorded against this node ever inflating, is that causal inference from displays is unreliable in both directions and is not fixed by richer drawing; over-reading is not the only failure and a better mark is not automatically a better inference. The fused-form hazard is measured: connected scatterplots — the clever combined encoding of paired time series — produce more order and direction confusions and fewer correlation reads than plain line graphs, while engaging viewers more (Haroz, Kosara & Franconeri 2016; engagement and accuracy kept separate as the authors do; their baseline's axis configuration was not verified, so no dual-axis comparison is asserted from it). Mix-effects remedies exist as design work: comet charts build the segment-weight decomposition into the mark itself so a mix shift is visible beside a value shift (Armstrong & Wattenberg 2014 — a documentation-and-technique paper; no controlled user study of it was found, and it is cited as remedy pattern, not reader evidence). Dual-axis superimposition, held at its honest weight: it is the most common design-guideline violation among misleading charts in the wild ('the use of dual axes (5.4% of all posts)' — Lisnic et al. 2023, an observational content analysis, not a reading experiment, whose own headline runs the other way: only ~12% of posts violate design guidelines at similar rates with and without reasoning errors, and incorrect chart reading was the least common reasoning error — a null that strengthens rather than weakens this clause), an active peer-reviewed defense of dual axes exists (Brath et al. 2020, expanded 2022), and no strong controlled experiment on two-MEASURE dual axes was found by the 2026-08-28 search — the folklore outruns the evidence, and the nearest-looking study is a trap recorded here so no later run miscites it: Isenberg et al. 2011 studied dual-SCALE charts (two resolutions of one measure, focus+context), found them confusing and recommended against superimposition, and says nothing about two measures on two y-axes. The two search-negatives that used to close this premise live at map-10 now, at the rung an absence honestly wears, together with the parked lead's 2026-09-01 disposition. Verification grade: all sources corroborated at search-index/abstract/snippet level against at least two independent index records (publisher full texts egress-blocked from this container, per the body and database lanes' precedent), grades labeled inline where they matter; Xiong's experiments 2–3 and Haroz's baseline configuration deliberately not asserted beyond what was verified; Lisnic's 5.4% given in the source's own wording.
sources: Xiong C, Shapiro J, Hullman J, Franconeri S 2020, 'Illusion of Causality in Visualized Data', IEEE TVCG 26(1):853-862, DOI 10.1109/TVCG.2019.2934399 — Exp 1 causality ratings highest for text and bar, weaker for scatter; Exps 2–3 aggregation-as-driver carried as the authors' summary, not read at full text (2026-08-28 search)

Kale A, Wu Y, Hullman J 2022, 'Causal Support: Modeling Causal Inferences with Visualizations', IEEE TVCG 28(1):1150-1160, DOI 10.1109/TVCG.2021.3114824 — insensitivity to sample size and greater sensitivity to disconfirming than confirming evidence, vs a Bayesian benchmark; no tested design beat plain text contingency tables

Haroz S, Kosara R, Franconeri SL 2016, 'The Connected Scatterplot for Presenting Paired Time Series', IEEE TVCG 22(9):2174-2186, PMID 26600062 — more order/direction confusions and fewer correlation reads than line graphs; higher engagement; baseline axis configuration not verified

Armstrong Z, Wattenberg M 2014, 'Visualizing Statistical Mix Effects and Simpson's Paradox', IEEE TVCG 20(12):2132-2141, DOI 10.1109/TVCG.2014.2346297, PMID 26356927 — design/technique paper (comet charts); no controlled user study found

Lisnic M et al. 2023, 'Misleading Beyond Visual Tricks: How People Actually Lie with Charts', CHI 2023, DOI 10.1145/3544548.3580910 — observational content analysis; dual axes the most common guideline violation ('5.4% of all posts', the source's own wording); the paper's own headline: guideline violations are rare and similar with and without reasoning errors

Brath R, Hagerman C, Sorenson E 2020, 'Why Two Y-Axes (Y2Y): A Case Study for Visual Correlation with Dual Axes', IV 2020 (IEEE Xplore 9373177); expanded 2022 as 'Dual Y Axes Charts Defended: Case Studies, Domain Analysis and a Method', in Kovalerchuk et al. (eds.), Integrating Artificial Intelligence and Visualization for Visual Knowledge Discovery, Studies in Computational Intelligence 1014, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-93119-3_22 — the peer-reviewed defense; case studies, not controlled experiments

Isenberg P, Bezerianos A, Dragicevic P, Fekete J-D 2011, 'A Study on Dual-Scale Data Charts', IEEE TVCG 17(12):2469-2478, PMID 22034368 — recorded as the trap: dual-SCALE (focus+context of one measure), not dual-measure; not evidence about two y-axes for two measures

nodes.claim: The strongest deployed display of within-person coupling rendered it as natural-language statements rather than drawn lines and reported the resulting insights highly variable between individuals; the deployed precedent beside it spans drawn correlation displays and the raw series.
nodes.detail: Fissioned out of map-6 on 2026-09-01 (central's 2026-08-28 question, carrying go-7); the text is map-6's 2026-08-28 precedent survey — design consequence (d)'s evidence half — adversarially checked before it first landed, carried here with its grades intact. All of it is display-of-within-person-coupling systems and methods work rather than reader experiments — Daza is a methods framework, not a deployed system — and it is cited as precedent, not as comprehension evidence. Personal cross-stream correlation display exists (SleepExplorer, 2016). The strongest deployed system rendered within-person correlations as natural-language statements rather than drawn lines, and reported the resulting insights highly variable between individuals (Health Mashups, 2013) — that language is a legitimate display channel for a coupling, and for low-n within-person couplings plausibly the honest one, is map-6's inference, drawn there. One tension held openly, with map-8: Xiong's text condition drew the HIGHEST causality ratings of the four forms, so language is not automatically safer — its honesty has to come from stating population and basis in the sentence, which is precisely what a sentence can do and an unlabeled mark cannot; this connects to map-4's record that plain-text quantile intervals outranked the PDF and interval displays on point estimates, orderings map-4 itself records as not reliably distinguished. ESM feedback work argues for showing the raw individual series rather than summary statistics (ESMvis, 2021); and N-of-1 counterfactual frameworks supply the conditioning-basis vocabulary for the personal half (Daza 2018; the related 'Person as Population' item is a preprint and is deliberately not cited as evidence). Newest adjacent precedent, checked 2026-09-01: CALTREND (arXiv 2505.00855, 'Beyond the Mirror: Personal Analytics through Visual Juxtaposition with Other People's Data', May 2025) juxtaposes one person's deidentified calendar logs with other people's — the you-beside-a-population shape (reading it as the Mirror's shape is this lane's own identification, not the paper's) — verified real at search-index/snippet grade; preprint, so recorded as design precedent only and deliberately not cited as evidence (map-10 holds its bearing on the search-negatives). Verification grade: all sources corroborated at search-index/abstract/snippet level against at least two independent index records (publisher full texts egress-blocked from this container, per the body and database lanes' precedent), grades labeled inline where they matter.

nodes.claim: No study was found showing readers map an aggregate display onto themselves individually; none testing whether readers distinguish within-person from between-person structure in a display; and, added 2026-09-02, none stating that one coordinate system should persist across levels of analysis, none testing readers across an individuals-to-density switch inside one coordinate system versus a separate view, none on network latency in phone-based visual analysis, and no published auditability argument for client-side rendering from aggregates — search-negatives, attacked, still standing.
nodes.detail: Split out of map-8 on 2026-09-01 at this run's adversarial pass's insistence: a universal negative is a search that found nothing — it can be attacked and survive, but no source can ground it, so it wears argued no matter how load-bearing it is, and keeping it inside a cited node was exactly the hand-label pathology go-7 names (an argued-rung sub-claim living inside a cited node). The two negatives, stated precisely: (1) no study was found showing readers map an aggregate display onto themselves individually — the product-shaped worry that a Mirror user reads the crowd's coupling as their own is map-6's inference from map-7's divergence plus InSight's juxtaposition of you and cohorts, stated there as inference; (2) no controlled study was found testing whether readers distinguish within-person from between-person structure in a display at all. Search record: the 2026-08-28 scout (one Opus web pass over the connection-reading literature, 16 sources verified) found neither; the 2026-08-28 adversarial pass attacked both deliberately and they held; the one lead that pass parked was checked 2026-09-01 — arXiv 2505.00855, 'Beyond the Mirror: Personal Analytics through Visual Juxtaposition with Other People's Data', is real, a cs.HC preprint (May 2025) presenting CALTREND, a visual-analytics system juxtaposing one person's deidentified online calendar logs with other people's (verified at search-index/snippet grade — web-search index snippets of the arXiv record; arXiv full text egress-blocked from this container) — juxtaposition design-precedent work (recorded at map-9), not a controlled comprehension experiment on population recovery or level discrimination, and preprint grade regardless; both negatives stand. Why the absence is load-bearing rather than trivia: if readers could be shown to recover an undeclared population unaided, map-6's declaration rule would be courtesy; nothing shows they can, so it is structure. Standing duty: any run touching this territory re-searches before restating these — a single controlled experiment either way moves this node, and its status can rise only if the negatives are ever converted into a cited positive finding about what readers do. ADDED 2026-09-02, at the adversarial pass's insistence and by this node's own rule (a universal negative wears argued, and keeping it inside a cited node is the hand-label pathology): four more negatives from this run's two scouts, each a web-search sweep of at least four queries with publisher and index APIs egress-blocked. (3) No source states that one coordinate system should persist across levels of analysis or across population cuts — map-1's rule is therefore this lane's composition, held at argued. (4) No controlled study tests readers' orientation or their reading of a variable across an individuals-to-density level-of-detail switch inside one coordinate system versus a separate aggregated view; nearest neighbours: Kim, Correll & Heer 2019 (identification of the aggregate operation, carried at map-11) and Phoenixmap (arXiv 2002.00732, dot maps versus heatmaps versus a novel density form — representations, not transitions). (5) No study of network round-trip latency on phone-based data-visualization use; nearest: device input-to-display touch-latency studies, one mobile web-search latency paper (arXiv 2101.09086), one mobile-AR latency paper — different tasks, none the missing experiment. (6) No published argument that visualizations computed client-side from published aggregates are thereby reader-verifiable; nearest: BioVisReport (PMC9233186, a static reproducible-visualization builder — a tool, not the argument) and reproducibility-stamp work on research artifacts — orthogonal. Load-bearing for: map-1 (3, 4), map-13 (4), map-5 and map-14 (5, 6). Same standing duty: any run touching these re-searches before restating; one controlled study either way moves the relevant clause.

nodes.claim: Multiscale navigation is a studied, modellable cost rather than a free property: a view with no navigational information is a named and analyzed navigation failure (desert fog), zoom-and-pan has a formal optimal-animation model with an explicit trade-off parameter, semantic zoom's reported wins differ by study (no correctness difference with better recall and preference in one map study; faster and less error-prone in one program-visualization study), aggregation across levels of detail carries design guidelines including one reported as discriminability of aggregates from items, and staged animated aggregation transitions help readers identify the operation performed.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-09-02 as the cited premise layer under map-1 and map-13 — the facts kept apart from the compositions that use them (the tst-6/tst-7 form). WHAT THE LITERATURE CARRIES. 'Desert fog' is a view of an information world containing no information on which to base navigational decisions, a named and analyzed navigation failure met with view-based aids and a critical-zone analysis grouping objects by visibility across views rather than by spatial layout (Jul & Furnas 1998 — definitions reported; a user study is not asserted). Crossing scales has a formal cost model: an optimal smooth zoom-and-pan animation derives analytically from a perceived-velocity metric with two free parameters, animation speed and the zoom/pan trade-off (van Wijk & Nuij 2003; journal form 2004) — modellable cost, not a normative claim of deliberate cost. Semantic zoom — representation changing with scale, the idea from Pad (Perlin & Fox 1993), the term from Pad++ — has been tested, with results that differ by study: on map tasks, overview+detail versus a zoomable interface showed no difference in task correctness, most participants preferred having an overview, and the multi-level (semantically zoomed) map gave richer navigation cues, made the overview unnecessary and improved recall of objects (Hornbæk, Bederson & Plaisant 2002); a program-visualization study found blended continuous semantic zooming faster and less error-prone than flat viewing (Summers et al. 2003). The taxonomy — overview+detail, zooming, focus+context and, at snippet grade, a fourth (cue-based) — is Cockburn, Karlson & Bederson's; its empirical verdict on which form wins is NOT asserted, because that section could not be reached and one candidate quotation was traced to a different paper (a UMD HCIL report). Aggregation across levels of detail has design guidelines whose reported names — single-listing snippet grade — include an entity budget, visual summary, discriminability ('aggregates should be distinguishable from individual items') and fidelity (counteracting artifacts that misrepresent true effects) (Elmqvist & Fekete 2010); that a seamless continuation of one mark would VIOLATE that guideline is map-13's inference from the name, not the paper's stated prohibition, and stands or falls on a primary read. Staged animated transitions improve accuracy at identifying which aggregate operation was performed, sometimes at a time cost (Kim, Correll & Heer 2019); unit visualizations — every data item its own mark — are a described grammar family whose mental-model advantage is stated as motivation, not a tested result (Park et al. 2018). What it does not carry lives at map-10 (the 2026-09-02 negatives), at the rung an absence wears. Verification grade: publisher and index APIs egress-blocked this run; every source corroborated on authors, title, venue, year and DOI by at least two independent index listings, page ranges and article numbers as printed in those listings and single-sourced unless noted; content at search-snippet grade, reported not read; no number asserted. Standing duty (§11): every sentence here is reported, not read; any of them contradicted by a primary read demotes this node loudly, and the run that reaches full text records which sentences survived.

nodes.claim: The telescope has exactly one seam of geometry, at the person — mark changes across the population stops are not seams — and zooming past the between-person point that is you crosses into a within-person geometry (one per state space) drawn as a declared transition; the seam vanishes for a pair of axes only when cross-level invariance is measured for it, never by assumption.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-09-02, split from map-1's revision so the ladder can grip it separately. The between-person telescope reaches its smallest cohort at n = 1: you are a point in the shared space, and a point has no coupling — crowd structure stops being drawable there. Your own coupling lives in the within-person geometry — one per state space, in cen-1's plural — whose loadings are estimated separately (cen-1; tst-6 part 3, on tst-7's cited facts: within-person variance two to four times the group estimate, cross-level generalization only under rarely met ergodicity). So drawing 'has your openness moved' as motion of your point along a between-person axis asserts a cross-level loading invariance the joint model must instead test. The perfect display therefore does not zoom past the person; it CROSSES: the step from the population space to your own is a declared change of geometry — different axes, different marks (a trajectory over occasions, map-6's within-person form), the population's item-directions no longer valid landmarks — drawn as a transition, never hidden as continuity. The mark changes along the population stops (map-13) are not seams: coordinates persist there, and here they do not. Conditional, not absolute: where tst-6's invariance test passes for a pair of axes, the two geometries coincide there and the seam vanishes for that pair — coincidence declared on measurement, never assumed. Consequence at the density level: the within-person geometry has an aggregate object too — the population-average within-person parameter (pat-3), an average OVER persons' dynamics and nobody's own (pat-8: another person's stream carries no information about yours beyond a group prior) — drawn as a second field, never as vectors on the between-person plane. Falsifiers: (a) cross-level loading invariance holding for ALL of InSight's axes — the seam would then have no domain and 'exactly one seam' would be an empty claim; or invariance failing for a pair while readers of a single continuous zoom through it show no measurable misreading; (b) a controlled study showing readers correctly read a within-person trajectory drawn on between-person axes — map-10 records that none on distinguishing the two levels in a display was found. To measured: the repeated measurements that tst-6's era-scoped re-serving request would create (needs-owner, bridge item 5 in DIGEST.md). Status argued: an architecture inference composed from cited siblings.

nodes.claim: Across the population stops the mark changes with cohort size and the space does not: one point, named unit marks with exact counts, an anonymous sample stated as such, then density over published bins with no per-person datum — a cohort is drawn as a density and never as a centroid, and thinness at world zoom is drawn as counts, empty where empty.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-09-02, fissioned from map-1's revision at the adversarial pass's request: a separable design claim with its own premises and falsifier. THE LADDER. n = 1: you, one point. Tens (circle): named unit marks, each carrying the exact agreement count the product already folds beside a name (docs/PEOPLE-MAP.md §2 on main). Hundreds (city): unit marks from a bounded, recency-capped sample, anonymous, with the cap stated when it binds — the honest bias the who-voted sheet already names. Thousands and up (country, world): density over published bins in the declared plane (map-1), no per-person datum, which is cen-1's publication rule — population-level sufficient statistics, never per-person latent draws — applied to the drawing, and what map-5 says the phone then draws. Continuity is of coordinates, never of mark: marks at different levels must look different, this lane's inference from the discriminability guideline map-11 reports at snippet grade (aggregates distinguishable from individual items), and the level switch itself is an aggregation the reader must recognize, which map-11's animated-transition result speaks to. A cohort is drawn as a DENSITY, never as a centroid point: an average person is closer to everyone than any person is, so a centroid in the person space would be a second meaning for distance (map-2) — 'what your city says about the world' is read as two densities in one basis, not two dots, and the product's Country and World stops, which arrange cities and countries as placed objects by score likeness, are the case this clause names. Thinness at world zoom looks like what it is: cells drawn frequency-framed with their counts (map-4's outcome-uncertainty form), empty where empty, never smoothed into a contour the n cannot carry; the perfect display would rather show a sparse grid than a confident cloud. Standing cost: aggregation raises perceived causality (map-8), so the density level invites over-reading, met by declaration in the frame (map-6), not avoided. Search record at map-10: no controlled study of readers across an individuals-to-density switch inside one coordinate system versus a separate view. Falsifier: readers shown an in-place level switch (units to bins in one fixed plane) misread the drawn variable more than readers shown the aggregate in a separate view — the ladder's in-place clause would fall, map-1's coordinate rule would not. Status argued: this lane's design inference over cited premises (map-4, map-8, map-11, cen-1 by edge).

nodes.claim: Interaction latency is behaviour, not polish — an added 500 ms delay reduced exploratory activity, coverage and the rate of observations and hypotheses, and blocking (not progressive) delivery is what degrades analysis — and binned aggregation is the published design principle under which rendering cost is bounded by the resolution of the visualized data rather than the number of records, with the field's own systems keeping a bounded server in the loop.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-09-02 as the cited premise layer under map-5, kept apart from the design conclusion that uses it. LATENCY. An added delay of 500 ms in an exploratory visual-analysis study decreased user activity and dataset coverage, reduced the rate at which users made observations, drew generalizations and generated hypotheses, and shifted exploration strategy, with early exposure to higher latency depressing later low-latency performance (Liu & Heer 2014 — an ADDED delay against a baseline, not a threshold; desktop, not mobile). The precise reading is against BLOCKING: with progressive, instantaneous and blocking conditions compared, users performed equally well with instantaneous or progressive results on insight-discovery rate and dataset coverage while blocking had detrimental effects (Zgraggen et al. 2017). AGGREGATION. The binned-aggregation principle — in reported wording, not read in a record — that perceptual and interactive scalability should be limited by the chosen resolution of the visualized data, not the number of records (imMens, Liu, Jiang & Heer 2013); the data-cube line (Nanocubes, Lins, Klosowski & Scheidegger 2013) and the prefetch-and-reindex line (Falcon, Moritz, Howe & Heer 2019) are the shapes per-view work takes when it is not zero — Nanocubes is a server-side index and Falcon reindexes on interaction, trading resolution for latency, so this node carries the literature's bounded server honestly rather than a zero it never claims. Search-negatives (map-10): no mobile visual-analysis latency study; no published auditability argument for client-side rendering from aggregates.
